newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New HK airport fees may nearly double - official.
newsitem.headline: New HK airport fees may nearly double - official.

text.p: Hong Kong's Airport Authority said on Friday it has proposed nearly doubling the charges airlines currently pay when the territory's new Chek Lap Kok airport opens in April 1998.
Henry Townsend, chief executive of the Airport Authority, also said airlines should be able to receive more information on what the charges were based on by the end of April.
"Our charges will be slightly less than twice than those now levied at the existing airport," Townsend told a business luncheon.
The authority is in charge of developing Hong Kong's new airport at Chek Lap Kok, scheduled to open in April 1998.
The charges include landing fees, parking fees and passenger terminal fees, he said, adding that cargo planes would not have to pay the passenger terminal fees.
He said the authority will be consulting with the International Air Transport Association (IATA) on the proposed charges.

Antony Tyler, director of corporate development of Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, who was also at the luncheon, declined to comment on the proposal. He said the airline needed a breakdown on the charges to decide if they were fair.
The Airport Authority (AA) and IATA held two days of talks earlier this week on user charges at Chek Lap Kok, following which IATA expressed disappointment.
"The AA have proposed substantially higher landing and parking chares," IATA said in a statement on Thursday.

"However, we have still not received a full charging schedule from the AA, and there are still some areas where they have not provided any indication on what the costs will be. This is very alarming to the airline community as we are still unable to assess the total increases," it said.
